title: Love-You Gesture Emoji 🤟 Meaning: “I Love You” in ASL
description: 🤟 is the American Sign Language sign for “I love you,” not the rock-on horns. Learn what the love-you gesture emoji means and how to tell it from 🤘.
summary: The 🤟 love-you gesture emoji means “I love you.” It shows the American Sign Language sign that combines the handshapes for I, L and Y into one: thumb, index finger and little finger extended. People send it to express love or affection, though many mistake it for the rock-and-roll horns.
meaning: The handshape comes from American Sign Language. Fingerspelled I is a raised pinky, L is an extended thumb and index finger, and Y is thumb and pinky out. Hold all three at once and you have ILY, a compact “I love you” that deaf and hearing signers alike use to greet family, say goodbye and show warmth across a room.

As an emoji it carries that message directly. Parents send it to children, partners to each other, and friends at the end of a call. It is a touch more casual than a red heart and has a distinctive, slightly knowing quality, since the recipient needs to recognize the sign. In Deaf community spaces online it is also used with pride as a marker of sign language and Deaf culture.

Confusion with 🤘 is constant. The only visual difference is the thumb: out for love, tucked in for horns. Plenty of people pick 🤟 to mean “rock on” at concerts and in music posts without noticing. That usage is widespread enough that context has to settle the matter. A message about a guitar solo means horns, and “night, mom” means love.

A third association is Spider-Man, whose web-shooting pose uses a similar hand position with the palm turned up. Fans sometimes use 🤟 for that, especially next to a spider or web emoji. It is a playful borrowing and has no connection to the sign's actual meaning, and the character's real pose bends the wrist back in a way the emoji does not show.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is a warm sign-off: “drive safe 🤟” or “proud of you 🤟.” Families with deaf or signing members use it routinely, and others pick it up as a low-key alternative to typing “love you.” It can feel less heavy than a heart for people who are affectionate but not gushy, such as siblings, old friends and dads.

contexts.label: From a crush or partner
contexts.body: From a partner who knows what it means, it is a straightforward “I love you.” From a crush, be careful about reading too much into it, because a large share of users think it is a rock or “cool” gesture. Look at what surrounds it. Next to hearts or a goodnight message it is affectionate, and next to a concert photo it is not a declaration.

contexts.label: In music and fandom
contexts.body: Despite its origin, it shows up all over festival captions, band fan pages and gig photos as an interchangeable version of the horns. Some users simply prefer its look. Marvel fans use it for Spider-Man's web-slinging hand. None of this is wrong enough to cause offense, but signers will read the love message first.

Affection for a partner or family member, reinforced with a heart.

examples.text: Thanks for always having my back 🤟

examples.meaning: A Spider-Man reference imitating his web-shooting hand.

combos.meaning: An unmistakable “I love you,” removing any confusion with rock horns.
Love plus a kiss; an affectionate goodbye.
Rock-on energy at a show, where the sender means the horns.

confusedWith.difference: 🤘 keeps the thumb folded over the middle fingers and means rock on, metal or excitement. 🤟 extends the thumb and means “I love you” in American Sign Language. One finger changes the message from affection to headbanging.
🤙 extends only the thumb and little finger, the shaka or “call me” sign. 🤟 adds a raised index finger. The shaka says hang loose, and the three-finger sign says I love you.
🫶 forms a heart shape with two hands and reads as love or gratitude to nearly everyone. 🤟 says the same thing in sign language but depends on the recipient recognizing it.

avoid: Do not assume everyone knows it means “I love you”; add a heart or words when the message matters.
Avoid sending it to casual acquaintances or colleagues if you only mean “rock on,” since some will read affection.
Do not use it to joke about sign language or deafness.
design: A raised hand with the thumb, index finger and little finger extended and the two middle fingers folded down, palm facing the viewer. All major platforms draw the same handshape, with small differences in angle. It was added in 2017, two years after the similar sign of the horns, and supports skin tones.

faqs.q: How can I tell 🤟 and 🤘 apart?
faqs.a: The thumb. With the thumb extended, 🤟 is the ASL sign for “I love you.” With the thumb tucked in, 🤘 is the sign of the horns used in rock and metal culture. They are frequently swapped by accident.

faqs.q: What does 🤟 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: If he knows the sign, he is saying “love you” in a relaxed way, to a partner, relative or close friend. Many guys use it as “rock on” or “cool,” however, so do not treat it as a confession without supporting evidence.

faqs.q: What does 🤟 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Usually affection, since it is the “I love you” sign, and it is often paired with hearts. As with anyone, she may be using it as a generic cool or rock gesture, so the rest of the message matters.

Not officially, but fans use it that way because it resembles his web-shooting hand. Spider-Man's version points the palm upward with the hand lowered. The emoji was designed to represent the sign language phrase.

faqs.q: Is the love-you gesture used outside American Sign Language?
faqs.a: The sign originated in ASL and is recognized by many hearing people in the United States. Other sign languages have their own ways to say “I love you,” so it is not universal, though the emoji has spread the gesture internationally.
